page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16, alongside AES cryptography and BMI2 instructions. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.ce4.2xlarge in the average tier for most processing tasks. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1576.19 and a multi-core score of 8311.36. Memory performance is mixed; while the read-only small block cached bandwidth is average at 465.3 GB/sec, the uncached large block read bandwidth is weak at 37.76 GB/sec. Passmark testing reveals weak performance in database operations and physics simulations. However, the instance maintains average throughput in static web serving at 7.57 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 8.03 million operations per second. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor levels for medium 7B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.ce4.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of local storage. The primary tradeoff is the weak uncached memory bandwidth and lower database operation scores, which may limit performance in highly intensive transactional databases. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power, making it a viable option for memory-intensive applications, caching layers like Redis, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference using small models.
